figures.title: RNA-seq candidate detection
figures.alt: Adapter trimming, alignment, candidate detection, control and sequence filtering, replicate quantification and editor comparison form a six-step RNA-seq workflow.
figures.caption: 36 libraries, nine groups and four biological replicates per group; GRCh38 with GENCODE v50. The original screening and recounting rules remain in the Model page. Candidate sites and editing profiles support planned training and evaluation.

figures.title: PUF-ESM specificity ranking
figures.alt: A 493-amino-acid PUF sequence feeds frozen ESM-2 scores and reference-centred one-hot features. Grouped inner validation selects Ridge settings, which predict three editing outputs, specificity and held-out ranks.
figures.caption: The original feature branches and three endpoint outputs are preserved. Grouped inner cross-validation selects settings using Spearman correlation; the held-out assessment contains 66 complete constructs, including Top30 comparison with random expectation.

figures.title: Structure-conditioned PUF nomination
figures.alt: The fixed PUF–RNA complex branches into all-position and TRM-only masks, each sampled with two pretrained inverse-folding models, screened and compared with measured constructs.
figures.caption: Each model and mask used 10,000 samples, temperature 0.5 and seed 111. The AiCE-inspired screen yielded 128 non-TRM and 10 TRM nominations, with 46 and 0 exact dual-model matches, respectively. Comparison used 81 measured constructs; nominations do not imply experimental validation.

figures.title: Structural hypotheses and assay feedback
figures.alt: A closed six-step cycle compares RNA contexts, audits structural models, screens single mutants, combines hits, tests within batches and updates designs around a conceptual protein–RNA complex.
figures.caption: The original six-step order and feedback connection are unchanged. RNA comparisons address the +1 base and sequence context; selection pairs preference with retained activity, and each batch uses its matched parental normalization. The central complex is schematic.
